claims.statement: The IC-Suite consists of four independently versioned toolchains: callidescope, codependix, codometer, and conformetry, each named for the command a user runs.
All four toolchains share a five-layer architectural spine: core → configuration → analysis → output → cli, with each layer depending only downward.
The core layer holds only domain vocabulary (result/finding types, error classes, enums, unions, analyzer/validator contracts) and never holds services, modules, or anything executable.
The configuration layer holds the config file schema, loading, defaults, override resolution, and CLI flag resolution, producing one resolved configuration object; it never holds domain result types.
The analysis layer holds what the tool actually does (per-suite names and shapes) and never holds rendering or command wiring.
The output layer holds every render target (JSON, markdown, mermaid, anchor blocks, destination routing, delivery) and never holds analysis.
The cli layer holds only *.command.ts modules and nothing else, never any logic.

The nx plugin layer (where it exists in callidescope, codependix, and conformetry) sits above cli and carries layer:cli tag, not a sixth layer tag, because it is a second host for the same underlying toolchain.
The core-versus-configuration test: if a type describes what the tool produced, it belongs in core; if it describes what the user wrote in <tool>.config.ts, it belongs in configuration.
The analysis layer deliberately does not converge on a shared name across toolchains; it is governed by the rule: one package per independently usable analyzer, named for what it analyzes.
The *-agents and *-examples packages carry no layer tag and are not in the runtime chain; they are non-publishable (agents travel via skills-lock.json, examples are fixtures, some broken on purpose).

Each suite's analysis layer packages are named per-suite: callidescope-graph; codependix-boundaries, file-imports, nestjs-modules, nx-projects; codometer-languages, measurement; conformetry-generation, languages, validation.

The 29 publishable packages across the four suites version independently using Nx Release with projectsRelationship: "independent", conventional commits determine semver bumps, and Nx Release cascades patch bumps to internal dependents (updateDependents: "auto").
Releases operate at two tiers: repository root release (semantic-release, fixed version, no npm publishes) and publishable packages release (nx release, independent versioning, per-package tags).

Three gates prevent non-publishable packages from reaching npm: private: true in manifest, orchestrator's projects filter in nx.json, and registry permissions; a package outside publishable set is held by the first two, never by only one.

No cross-toolchain @ic-suite/* shared package is created; the common ConfigurationService shape is a convention, not an imported type — each toolchain's core declares its own structurally identical shape.

codependix-nx-projects is an analysis-layer graph builder that reads the Nx project graph, not an Nx plugin; it keeps its name despite colliding with the nx plugin layer namespace, documented as a deliberate exception.
callidescope measures call-stack depth (longest chain of nested calls) and breadth (fan-out: number of direct callees per callable) for every traced entry point in a project and its Nx dependencies.

callidescope CLI command accepts --check depth,breadth,reports to gate findings, --write to write reports, and --format to control stdout output; per-project config declares explicit maximumDepth and maximumBreadth limits.

callidescope Nx plugin infers four targets: callidescope-trace, callidescope-depth, callidescope-breadth, and callidescope-gate; the gate fails only on findings charged to the project itself, not its dependencies.

codependix measures three graph levels (file imports, NestJS modules, Nx projects) and validates forbid/allow boundary rules plus cycle detection; rules are defined in configuration/codependix.config.ts under boundaries with generic layer:* rules and per-package name:* rules.
codependix CLI command map accepts --check boundaries,reports, --write to regenerate README exports, and --format for output; --check boundaries gates every PR, --check reports gates default branch.
codependix Nx plugin infers codependix-gate target; graphs are built over the project and its dependencies, and only violations charged to the project itself fail its gate.

codometer measures file sizes (lines, bytes), symbol counts (functions, classes, methods, static methods), and comment-block word counts per language; custom counters for project conventions (Module Files, Service Files, Unit Tests, etc.).

codometer CLI command measure accepts --check limits to gate breaches, --output-json for JSON report, --output-markdown for README badges, and --inputs to override globs; shared config defines zero-tolerance limits on comment budgets.

codometer Nx target defined in nx.json has check and write configurations; check runs measure --check limits and fails on breaches, write updates README badges; build-projects depends on codometer so size limits gate builds.

conformetry validates generated code against templates using language-aware similarity scoring (0-100); workspace config at configuration/conformetry.config.ts defines generator groups with templates, input schemas, instance globs, and thresholds.
conformetry CLI validate command accepts --check to fail on threshold breaches, --templates and --instances to narrow scope; generate command scaffolds new files with interactive prompts.
conformetry Nx plugin infers conformetry-validate target; gate fails when instance score falls below group threshold; generated code (shadcn) is excluded via SHADCN_GENERATED_PATTERNS.

guard-code aggregator target in nx.json depends on callidescope-gate, codependix-gate, conformetry-validate, and other checks; build-projects aggregator depends on build and codometer so size limits gate packaging.

CI gate flow runs two separate paths: (1) nx affected -t guard-code executes callidescope-gate, codependix-gate, and conformetry-validate in parallel per affected project plus workspace integrity checks (catalog-manifests, lockfile, project-ports, readme-projects, vscode-extensions); (2) nx affected -t build-projects executes build and codometer:check (codometer measure --check limits) so size limits gate packaging. Findings are charged per-project and aggregated into GitHub status checks.
